questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake may also affect BAC.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Avoid placing items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because drivers will see you easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors.
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, you should stay ________ behind the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance in poor road or weather conditions.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look toward where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle-car crashes are caused by drivers failing to give the right-of-way to riders?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because drivers fail to give the right-of-way to riders.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed in addition to a helmet.
Not needed if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can harm your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection guards against damage while letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, ride in the left portion of your lane. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of spaces.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: A rider without a helmet is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Switch between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping, even for normal stops.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoids other drivers' blind spots, avoids road hazards, and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see the roadway through vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in heavy traffic, at night, in bad weather, or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean that way.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase it to at least three seconds in bad weather or poor conditions.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is following you too closely?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. This warns them that you are slowing down.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind. For larger animals, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, is pairing up with another rider a good idea?

options.text: Yes, to keep the group together.
No, because it blocks your escape routes.
No, because it makes motorcycles look like a car to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it blocks your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in pairs. Riding side by side blocks each rider's escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: To avoid fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Limit how far you ride each day.

questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue, dress for the weather, limit riding to about six hours per day, and take a break every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can happen when they wear off.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work properly?

options.text: Not allow for eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Restrict your vision to the sides.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely. It should also have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear side vision, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you from injury in a crash. It also protects you from weather like hot and cold. It does not cause discomfort.

questions.question: What happens if you brake while turning in a curve?

options.text: It will be the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be careful. As the motorcycle leans to turn, the tires use traction for the turn. This leaves less traction available for braking.

questions.question: When your weight moves forward while braking, what can you do?

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should lessen the amount of pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel has more traction. This means you can press the front brake harder.
